quizName:
DMV Practice Test  #4
										  					
  

25 Questions • Passing Score 19

questions.question: What commonly causes traffic accidents?

options.text: Not paying attention while driving
Driving too fast for the conditions
Following other vehicles too closely
All of the above

questions.correctAnswerText: All of the above
questions.explanation: Driving too fast causes many crashes. Not paying attention can lead to hitting other vehicles. Most rear-end collisions happen because drivers follow too closely.

questions.question: How does alcohol affect your driving skills and judgment?

options.text: It improves driving skills but hurts your judgment.
It hurts both driving skills and judgment.
It does not affect driving skills or judgment.
It does not affect judgment but hurts driving skills.

questions.correctAnswerText: It hurts both driving skills and judgment.
questions.explanation: Alcohol slows your reaction time and makes it harder to see clearly. It also affects your judgment about speed and distance. Alcohol lowers your caution and makes you take more risks.

questions.question: What does this road sign mean?

options.text: The road widens ahead.
The right lane is ending soon.
A highway entrance ramp is ahead.
The left lane is ending soon.

questions.correctAnswerText: The right lane is ending soon.
questions.explanation: This sign tells you that the right lane will end ahead.

questions.question: When you see a green traffic light, what should you do?

options.text: Keep driving unless vehicles or pedestrians are in the intersection.
Stop if a police officer is nearby.
Treat it like a four-way stop.
Come to a complete stop before going.

questions.correctAnswerText: Keep driving unless vehicles or pedestrians are in the intersection.
questions.explanation: At a green light, yield to pedestrians and vehicles still in the intersection. You can continue, but drive at a speed where you can stop if the light changes.

questions.question: What should you do when an aggressive driver approaches you?

options.text: Don't make eye contact, slow down, and let them pass.
Cut them off to slow them down.
Tailgate them.
Show them you disapprove of their behavior.

questions.correctAnswerText: Don't make eye contact, slow down, and let them pass.
questions.explanation: Stay calm and create distance between you and the aggressive driver. Slow down and let them pass. Do not make eye contact or make rude gestures.

questions.question: How should a seat belt be adjusted?

options.text: Loosely
Snug across your hip bones and lower belly
Hidden under the seat
Just enough to turn off the buzzer

questions.correctAnswerText: Snug across your hip bones and lower belly
questions.explanation: The lap belt should fit snugly across your hip bones and lower belly. The shoulder belt should sit comfortably so you can fit your fist between the belt and your chest.

questions.question: What should you do when driving near a blind pedestrian with a white cane or guide dog?

options.text: Slow down and be ready to stop.
Take the right-of-way.
Drive normally.
Drive away quickly.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down and be ready to stop.
questions.explanation: When you see a blind pedestrian with a white cane or guide dog, you must slow down and give them the right-of-way. Be ready to stop to protect them from harm.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: No right turn
You must turn right.
Watch for traffic on your right.
Don't park on the right side of the street.

questions.correctAnswerText: No right turn
questions.explanation: A red circle with a line through a symbol means you cannot do that action. In this case, you cannot turn right.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Pedestrians are walking on the road ahead.
A pedestrian crossing is ahead.
Pedestrians must not cross here.
Watch for construction workers on the road.

questions.correctAnswerText: A pedestrian crossing is ahead.
questions.explanation: This sign warns you that pedestrians may cross the road ahead. Drive carefully in this area.

questions.question: If you are in an accident, what should you do?

options.text: Stop immediately.
Help the injured.
Call the police.
All of the above

questions.correctAnswerText: All of the above
questions.explanation: Stop your vehicle right away. Move it out of traffic if you can. Call the police and ask for an ambulance if needed. Help with serious bleeding by applying pressure. Wait for emergency vehicles.

questions.question: What can cause distracted driving?

options.text: Eating, drinking, or smoking.
Talking or texting on a cell phone.
Changing the radio station or CD.
All of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: All of the above.
questions.explanation: Drivers must focus completely on driving. Any extra activity can distract you and create danger.

questions.question: If your car breaks down on a highway, what should you do?

options.text: Stay in your car and wait for help.
Turn on your four-way flashers to warn other drivers.
Honk your horn at passing cars.
Flash your headlights at oncoming traffic.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn on your four-way flashers to warn other drivers.
questions.explanation: Turn on your hazard flashers and move as far off the road as possible. Lift your hood so other drivers know your vehicle needs help.

questions.question: If a crossing guard is directing traffic in a school zone, you must:

options.text: Follow the directions given by the crossing guard.
Do what the other drivers are doing, even if the guard says otherwise.
Assume the guard should not be directing traffic.
Follow the normal rules as if no children were present.

questions.correctAnswerText: Follow the directions given by the crossing guard.
questions.explanation: Always follow directions from a crossing guard or law enforcement officer. Slow down and be extra careful in school zones.

questions.question: When you approach a steady red traffic light, you should:

options.text: Drive through if there is no other traffic.
Keep driving because you have the right-of-way.
Stop only if a police officer is nearby.
Come to a complete stop.

questions.correctAnswerText: Come to a complete stop.
questions.explanation: A red light means you must stop completely. Running a red light is illegal and dangerous. You may turn right on red only if a sign does not forbid it.

questions.question: When a school bus stops with its stop arm extended, you should:

options.text: Come to a complete stop and wait to proceed.
Honk your horn before passing the bus on the left.
Keep driving once you think most kids have exited the bus.
Pass the bus before its door opens.

questions.correctAnswerText: Come to a complete stop and wait to proceed.
questions.explanation: You must stop completely when a school bus has its stop arm out. Do not move until the stop arm is pulled in.

questions.question: What are the most effective safety restraints in a crash?

options.text: Only a lap and shoulder belt.
Only an airbag.
Both a lap and shoulder belt and an airbag.
No safety restraints.

questions.correctAnswerText: Both a lap and shoulder belt and an airbag.
questions.explanation: Safety belts greatly increase your chance of surviving a crash and avoiding serious injury. Airbags work best when used with safety belts. Always wear both your shoulder and lap belts.

questions.question: Highway markings:

options.text: Are usually not important.
Are only found in construction zones.
Give drivers important information.
Are usually red and blue in color.

questions.correctAnswerText: Give drivers important information.
questions.explanation: Road markings help you position your vehicle correctly, show where it is safe to pass, and warn you of upcoming hazards.

questions.question: When borrowing an unfamiliar vehicle from a friend, you should:

options.text: Not worry about it because all vehicles work the same way.
Hide from your friend that you don't know the vehicle.
Ignore any problems to avoid embarrassing your friend.
Take a few minutes to learn where the controls are and how they work before you drive.

questions.correctAnswerText: Take a few minutes to learn where the controls are and how they work before you drive.
questions.explanation: Before driving an unfamiliar vehicle, learn the location and operation of the turn signals, hazard lights, headlights, wipers, brakes, gear selector, and horn. Fix any problems before driving.

questions.question: If another driver cuts you off in traffic, you should:

options.text: Pull next to the driver and yell at them.
Let it go.
Flash your high beams at them.
Cut them off in return.

questions.correctAnswerText: Let it go.
questions.explanation: To avoid road rage, don't take it personally if another driver cuts you off. Just stay calm and keep driving safely.

questions.question: This sign means:

options.text: Stop.
Side road ahead.
Two-way left turn.
Farm machinery.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop.
questions.explanation: Eight-sided signs mean you must stop and check for other traffic before proceeding. Only go when it is safe.

questions.question: You should not follow other cars too closely because:

options.text: You may not see the road between the cars.
You may not have time to stop if the car in front slows or stops suddenly.
You may not see the car's turn signals.
You may not see the other car's brake lights.

questions.correctAnswerText: You may not have time to stop if the car in front slows or stops suddenly.
questions.explanation: If you follow too closely and the car in front slows or stops suddenly, you may not have enough time to avoid hitting it.

questions.question: Which of these statements is true about seat belts and child restraints?

options.text: Never place an infant or small child in the front seat of a car with airbags.
Airbags can be dangerous to infants and small children, even in low-speed crashes.
Always make sure all passengers use a seat belt or child restraint.
All of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: All of the above.
questions.explanation: Before you drive, fasten your seat belt and make sure all passengers use seat belts or child restraints. Seat belts greatly reduce your chance of injury or death in a crash. Children age 12 and under should ride in a rear seat with proper restraints. Never put a rear-facing infant seat in the front seat of a car with an airbag.

questions.question: Before changing lanes, you should:

options.text: Check your side mirror.
Check your rearview mirror.
Quickly turn your head to check for other cars.
All of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: All of the above.
questions.explanation: Before changing lanes, check your side and rearview mirrors for traffic behind you. Just before you move to the other lane, glance over your shoulder to check for cars in your blind spot.

questions.question: When you leave your car unattended, you must:

options.text: Turn off the engine.
Lock the ignition and remove the key.
Set the parking brake.
All of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: All of the above.
questions.explanation: When you leave your car unattended, you must turn off the engine, lock the ignition, remove the key, and set the parking brake.

questions.question: Drivers who drink alcohol before driving:

options.text: Always know the risks they are taking.
Cannot control their bodies, minds, or vehicles properly.
Are better drivers because they are more careful than sober drivers.
Have faster reaction times.

questions.correctAnswerText: Cannot control their bodies, minds, or vehicles properly.
questions.explanation: Alcohol damages judgment, vision, concentration, and reaction time. It is never safe to drink any amount of alcohol before driving.
